title: Hill Stations in Himachal Pradesh: Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala and More

metaDescription: Himachal Pradesh's hill stations compared: Shimla, Kufri, Narkanda, Manali, Dharamshala, Palampur, Dalhousie, Kasauli and quieter valleys, with seasons and routes.
description: A guide to the hill stations of Himachal Pradesh: Shimla with Kufri, Chail and Narkanda; Manali and the Kullu valley; Dharamshala, McLeod Ganj, Palampur and Bir in the Kangra valley; Dalhousie and Khajjiar; Kasauli; and quieter valleys such as Tirthan and Jibhi, with how they compare, seasons, getting there and routes.
dek: Himachal has more hill stations within easy reach of Delhi and Chandigarh than any other state. Here is how to choose.

hero.alt: Solang valley near Manali, Himachal Pradesh

intro: Himachal Pradesh runs from the Shivalik foothills to the high Himalaya, and its hill stations sit mostly in the middle ranges between about 1,500 and 2,500 m. Shimla, the former summer capital, and Manali, the gateway to Lahaul, are the best known; the Kangra valley (Dharamshala, McLeod Ganj, Palampur, Bir) and the Chamba hills (Dalhousie, Khajjiar) offer something quieter.
Beyond the hill stations lie the high valleys of Kinnaur, Lahaul and Spiti, covered in our mountain destinations guide.
quickAnswer: The main hill stations in Himachal Pradesh are Shimla (with Kufri, Chail and Narkanda nearby), Manali, Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj, Palampur, Dalhousie and Khajjiar, and Kasauli; Tirthan, Jibhi and Bir are quieter valley bases. March to June and October to November are the best months; December to February brings snow to higher places, while July to September has landslide risk.
takeaways: Shimla and Kasauli are the closest to Chandigarh and Delhi.
Manali is the base for Solang, the Atal Tunnel and Lahaul; Rohtang Pass needs a permit and opens in summer.
The Kangra valley combines Tibetan culture in McLeod Ganj with tea gardens in Palampur and paragliding at Bir.
Narkanda and Kufri hold snow longer than Shimla in winter.
Avoid the heaviest monsoon weeks, when landslides close roads.

items.name: Kufri, Chail and Narkanda
body: Kufri's slopes near Shimla, Chail's forests and old palace, and Narkanda's apple orchards and Hatu Peak; Narkanda often holds winter snow longest.

items.name: Kasauli
body: A small, quiet cantonment town above Kalka.

items.name: Manali
body: Old Manali, the Hadimba temple, Vashisht, Solang valley, and the Atal Tunnel to Sissu in Lahaul; Kasol and the Parvati valley nearby.

items.name: Dharamshala, Palampur and Bir
body: McLeod Ganj and the Tsuglagkhang, the Triund trail, Palampur's tea gardens and Bir's paragliding.

items.name: Dalhousie and Khajjiar
body: Colonial Dalhousie and the meadow at Khajjiar, ringed by deodar forest.

items.name: Tirthan and Jibhi
body: River stays near the Great Himalayan National Park and the Jalori Pass.

sections.heading: Getting there
list: Chandigarh (air and rail) is the gateway to Shimla, Kasauli and, by road, Manali.
Kalka is the start of the Kalka-Shimla toy train.
Bhuntar airport serves Kullu and Manali; Gaggal airport serves Dharamshala; flights are limited and weather-dependent.
Overnight Volvo buses run from Delhi to Shimla, Manali and Dharamshala.

sections.heading: A little history
paras: Shimla became the summer capital of British India in 1864, which is why its Ridge, Mall Road and churches look the way they do. Dalhousie, Kasauli and Dharamshala grew as cantonments and sanatoriums in the same era. After 1959, McLeod Ganj became home to the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government in exile, and the town's Tibetan culture is now its main draw. Long before any of this, the Kullu valley's village temples and the Kangra school of painting were the region's heritage.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Stay near the Ridge in Shimla for walkability, or in Mashobra, Chail or Narkanda for quiet. In Manali, Old Manali and Vashisht have guesthouses and cafés, while the Naggar side of the valley is calmer. McLeod Ganj has budget stays and Dharamkot is quieter above it. In winter, confirm heating and road access.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to June: pleasant and busy; book ahead for May and June.
July to September: monsoon rain and frequent landslides; not ideal.
October to November: clear views and quieter towns.
December to February: cold; snow is likely around Manali, Solang, Kufri and Narkanda, less reliably in Shimla town.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
packing: Warm layers and a waterproof jacket

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in Himachal Pradesh?
faqs.a: Shimla and Manali are the most popular; Dharamshala, Dalhousie and Kasauli are quieter.

faqs.q: Which Himachal hill station is closest to Delhi?
faqs.a: Kasauli and Shimla, about 300 to 350 km by road.

faqs.q: Where can I see snow in Himachal?
faqs.a: Solang near Manali, Kufri and Narkanda near Shimla, and higher areas in mid-winter, though snowfall varies.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Rohtang Pass?
faqs.a: Yes; permits are issued online and the pass opens in summer. The Atal Tunnel needs no permit.

faqs.q: Is Himachal safe in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Landslides are common in July and August; keep plans flexible and check road updates.
